Gen 20 has no time cue to date it. I chain it on Gen 19's last Abraham scene (19:27-28) with a wide margin. Mamre as starting point is inferred from 18:1 and 19:27; the text only says 'from there'. notes.note: All verses 1-18 are covered. Verse 18 is placed with the healing (17-18) as its explanation, though the closing of the wombs began with the taking.

Gen 21:1-2 (Sarah conceives and bears Isaac) likely follows from the healing and the closed wombs of Gen 20:18; that chapter's session should consider a link, and note that Abraham's age at Isaac's birth (100) is bounded by anchor.isaac_birth. Abraham's age is 99 in Gen 17:24 and no age is given in Gen 20.

[entity:person.abimelech.gen_20_2] Already defined in the corpus (from GEN.26, where he is the later king of Gerar). I reuse the same entity for the Abimelech of Gen 20 because the registry gives one TIPNR id (Abimelech@Gen.20.2-) to both; many scholars treat them as distinct rulers or a dynastic title, but the corpus keeps one entity.

[entity:deity.yhwh] Elohim (20:3, 6, 13, 17) and Yahweh (20:18) both map to deity.yhwh, per the skill rule that a divine title is the deity. In 20:13 the plural verb with Elohim ('they caused me to wander') is still read of the one God.
